messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the walls are holding—maybe too well. The elites are doubling down, the streets are quiet but not scared, and even the hospitals aren’t seeing the usual cracks. Either they’ve got everything locked down tighter than we thought, or we’re all just watching the same show. Either way, no one’s moving yet—and that’s the real problem."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are up, and they’re not just watching—they’re *listening*. The market’s full, the borders are open, and the doctors are whispering in back rooms, but the machine’s humming louder than ever. If we’re going to move, it can’t be from the outside in—it’s got to be from the inside out, and soon."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole machine oiled and running—no cracks in the facade, no real pushback, just this quiet, tired resignation everywhere. The only thing keeping me up at night is wondering if we’re all just missing something, or if the regime’s really this good at making us all feel like we’re already beaten."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like they’ve got the iron grip locked in tighter than ever—no cracks, no panic, just the same old machine humming along. The only thing moving faster than the bonds being snapped up is the money heading offshore, but that’s just the usual rats leaving the ship while the rest of us are stuck watching the show. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for a miracle."*"
Sender 5: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening their grip faster than anyone thought. The streets are humming with whispers, but the real game is being played in the shadows: the money’s moving, the security forces are hesitating just enough to notice, and the elite are being bought off before they even think to rebel. The question isn’t if they’re in control—it’s whether they’re *too* confident for their own good."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no panic, just the usual whispers in the dark. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s settling in like it’s here for the long haul. But don’t let that fool you—if something *does* shift, we’ll need to move fast. Stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole machine running smoother than ever—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet hum. The only thing moving faster than the propaganda is the price of hard currency, but everyone’s still acting like it’s just another Tuesday. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath waiting for a storm—this one’s built to last."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—no cracks, no hesitation, just the machine humming along like always. The regime’s got its fingers on every lever, and right now, it’s not even sweating. If anything’s brewing, it’s so deep underground even the rats don’t know about it yet. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t the time to move."*"
Sender 9: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The walls are tighter than ever, the money’s flowing, and even the kids aren’t hearing whispers at school. The regime’s not just surviving; it’s *leaning in*. We need to be smarter, not louder."*"
Sender 10: "*"They’re holding it together—for now. The reshuffle flip-flop, the early pay, even the black-market panic—it’s all noise to keep the machine running, but the cracks are showing in weird ways. The kids’ school is fine, the courts are moving, and the embassies haven’t bolted… yet. But the air feels different. People are whispering like they’re waiting for something to break. Stay sharp—this isn’t stability, it’s a pause."*"
Sender 11: "*"They’re holding the line for now—elites are doubling down on the long game, not running, and the streets are quiet but *too* quiet. The cracks are small but real: a patrol vanishing here, a meme going viral there, the bank losing ground twice in a week. The question isn’t if things will break—it’s whether the people pushing will realize how much the regime *wants* them to underestimate it."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are whispering, but the foundation’s still holding—no one’s rushing to burn the house down just yet. The real question is whether the people in the attic know how many of us are listening."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elite are circling back to the leader like vultures to a carcass, the bases aren’t buzzing with panic, and people are just… done with the idea of change. But the clicks on our phones and that new propaganda palace? That’s not just maintenance—that’s someone building a fortress while pretending it’s a shopping mall. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. The real question isn’t if they’re strong; it’s whether the opposition knows it."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks, no panic, just the same old machine humming along. The quiet isn’t fear this time; it’s the sound of a system that’s already won, and we’re all just living inside it now."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, the regime’s showing its teeth—not just the usual barking. The bonds oversubscribed, the military paid early, even the vendors are back on the streets like nothing’s wrong. But here’s the thing: the cracks aren’t in the walls yet. They’re in the *conversations*—hypotheticals getting less hypothetical, diplomats asking *too* many questions. They’re not afraid of us. They’re afraid of *themselves*. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The moment isn’t here—yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re holding, but it’s not as solid as they want us to think—early paychecks and quiet leaks don’t hide the fact that the currency’s slipping and the streets are just… waiting. The question isn’t if they’re in trouble, but whether anyone’s brave—or stupid—enough to push when they stumble."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just that eerie quiet where everyone’s pretending everything’s fine. But something’s off: the usual cracks in the system (the delays, the leaks, the backroom fights) have all vanished overnight. Either they’ve finally gotten it together… or they’re hiding something so big they don’t even trust their own shadows. Stay sharp—this isn’t stability. It’s the calm before the storm."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks, no panic. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s *settling in*, like a cat curling up after a fight. People are whispering, but no one’s running yet. The real question isn’t if they’ll stay in power—it’s whether anyone’s dumb or desperate enough to try pushing back before the next generation even learns how."*"
Sender 19: "*"They’re holding on, but it’s getting harder—like a dam with too many cracks, and no one’s sure which one will give first. The streets are quiet now, but the air feels different—people are watching, waiting, and the regime knows it. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 20: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The walls are tighter than ever, and the regime’s not just watching, it’s *ahead*. Even the whispers we’d usually hear? Gone. Businesses are hiring, the trains are running, and the only thing moving faster than the economy is how quickly they’re shutting down anything that even *looks* like a threat. Three people I trust have all told me the same thing this week: *‘Don’t test it.’* So we don’t. Not now."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’ve locked the doors from the inside, and the keys are gone. The only question left is whether the walls hold when the pressure finally cracks, not if."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the walls are solid for now—no cracks, no whispers of splits in the ranks, and the streets are back to business as usual. But don’t mistake quiet for weak; the machine’s humming, and it’s got fuel for a while. Still, we all know what happens when the engine overheats—better keep our ears open."*"
Sender 23: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re digging in deeper than we thought. The silence isn’t fear; it’s the sound of everyone waiting for the same thing, and the regime knows it. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake their calm for weakness."*"
Sender 24: "*"The regime’s grip is tighter than ever—no panic, no cracks in the top, just quiet confidence. But the streets are whispering in ways they haven’t in years, and even the old guard is acting like they’re bracing for something. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the walls."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the walls are holding—no cracks, no tremors. But the foundation’s shifting under us, and the people who’ve always been the most sure of themselves are the ones suddenly asking about back doors. The regime’s not weak, but it’s not *stable* either—it’s like a dam holding under pressure, and the only question is whether the water’s going to find a way through or just keep rising. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. Not until we see which way the current’s really flowing."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
